title: Procedural by-law changes for appointed regional chair
subtitle: Accessibility advisory committee refresh, township representation, and a deferred health centre development charges grant request.
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended that Council adopt a new Regional Procedural By-law, to take effect November 15, 2026, when the Region becomes a municipality with a strong head of council {{vote:m2}}. Councillors first rejected a proposal to delay it until the new term {{vote:m3}}. Council is expected to consider the by-law on October 14, 2026, after public notice.

The committee also recommended adopting refreshed Terms of Reference for the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee. Staff are to report to Council on September 23 with wording to ensure at least one member is appointed from the area townships {{vote:m4}}. This affects how residents with disabilities can take part in advising the Region.

After waiving notice, the committee considered a request for a grant of $81,681.86 to Woolwich Community Health Centre to cover the Regional development charges on its expansion. It recommended deferring the request to the 2027 budget process as a possible addition {{vote:m8}}. The committee also met in closed session on legal advice about security of property at 150 Frederick Street, Kitchener.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that the Clerk give public notice of Council's intent, on October 14, 2026, to repeal the current procedural by-law and approve the new one effective November 15, 2026 {{vote:m2}}.
The committee defeated a motion to defer the by-law until the new term of Council and receipt of the provincial mandate {{vote:m3}}.

The committee recommended adopting the refreshed Terms of Reference and asked staff to report to Council on September 23 with language ensuring at least one member from the area townships {{vote:m4}}.
The committee recommended deferring the requested grant to the 2027 budget process as a proposed addition, rather than deciding it now {{vote:m8}}.

debate: On deferring the procedural by-law, supporters said approving it early amounted to obeying in advance and that councillors should keep objecting to an appointed chair until the mandate letter is seen. Opponents said the by-law was largely procedural, that the Municipal Act applies regardless, and that deferral would gain nothing.

Staff said the one time-sensitive part is the provision for an acting chair if the province has not appointed a chair by November 15. An acting chair would not have strong-chair powers. Staff said the appointment is expected before then.

Councillors asked for plain-language public information and orientation training on the new powers. One councillor said the Region should not explain the powers, since that is a provincial responsibility. Others raised that an appointed chair answers to the province rather than voters.

On the accessibility committee, staff said a minimum township seat could be hard to fill if no one applies. A councillor argued the Region needs township representation and that staff could reserve one of the voting seats. Another said this seemed to recreate the previous joint arrangement.

On the health centre grant, staff said it would set a precedent and has no reserve to draw on, so the cost would fall on the tax levy and user rates. Supporters stressed the need for local primary care and the centre's links to Regional services. Others wanted funding sources and the 2027 budget context first.
